questions.question: Which Act created the post of the Governor-General of Bengal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Regulating Act, 1773**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Regulating Act, 1773**: This act was passed by the British Parliament to address the governance and financial issues in the East India Company. It created the post of **Governor-General of Bengal**, who was vested with significant administrative powers.
 
• The first Governor-General of Bengal was **Warren Hastings**, appointed under the provisions of this act. His office symbolized the centralization of power in British India.
 
• The act introduced a council of four members to assist the Governor-General, marking the beginning of structured British administration in India. *Hence, the Regulating Act, 1773 is the correct answer.*
 
• The Regulating Act also laid the foundation for the **Supreme Court of Calcutta**, established in 1774, which was the first British court in India.
 
• The act was a significant step in reforming the East India Company's governance and marked the beginning of Parliamentary control over its operations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other Important Acts:**

 
 
• **Pitt's India Act, 1784**: This act further enhanced British control over the East India Company by establishing a dual system of governance with the creation of the **Board of Control**. It did not create the post of Governor-General.
 
• **Government of India Act, 1858**: This act abolished the East India Company and transferred the governance of India directly to the British Crown. It created the post of **Viceroy of India**, not Governor-General of Bengal.
 
• **Charter Act, 1813:** This act renewed the East India Company's charter but allowed other traders to participate in trade with India. It did not create any new administrative posts like Governor-General.
 
 
 
• **Governor-General of Bengal:**
 
 
• The position was later upgraded to **Governor-General of India** in 1833 by the **Charter Act of 1833**, centralizing authority further.
 
• The Governor-General was responsible for implementing British policies and maintaining control over territories in India.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court of Calcutta:**
 
 
• Established under the Regulating Act, 1773, the Supreme Court of Calcutta marked the beginning of a formal British judicial system in India.
 
• It had jurisdiction over British subjects in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics of Regulating Act, 1773:**

 
 
• The act introduced Parliamentary control over the East India Company, marking a significant shift in governance.
 
• It sought to address corruption and mismanagement within the company and improve accountability.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Governor-General:**
 
 
• The Governor-General of Bengal played a crucial role in centralizing British administration, eventually leading to the establishment of the Governor-General of India.
 
• This position was pivotal in implementing British policies and maintaining their control over Indian territories.

questions.question: At the time of independence, which sector contributed the largest share to India's national income?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• At the time of **India’s independence in 1947**, the **agriculture sector** contributed the largest share to the national income. It was the backbone of the Indian economy during this period.
 
• Agriculture accounted for nearly **50% of the national income** in India at the time of independence. This dominance was because of the large rural population and dependence on farming.
 
• The majority of the Indian population, approximately **70%-75%**, lived in rural areas and relied on agriculture for their livelihood. Hence, the sector played a crucial role in the economy.
 
• During colonial rule, India's economy was primarily agrarian, and industries were underdeveloped due to the lack of proper investments and infrastructure. Thus, trade, industry, and services contributed less to the national income compared to agriculture.
 
• The **British colonial policies** focused on exploiting India’s agricultural resources for their benefit, which further reinforced the agricultural dominance in the economy.
 
• Post-independence, while agriculture contributed the largest share to the national income, efforts were made to diversify the economy and develop industries and services.
 
• Even though agriculture was the primary contributor at independence, its share in the economy gradually declined with the growth of the industrial and service sectors over the subsequent decades.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Agriculture.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Significance of Agriculture in India’s Economy:**

 
 
• Agriculture has been the **foundation of India's economy** for centuries, supporting the livelihood of millions.
 
• At independence, India lacked industrial development, and agriculture was the **primary source of income** for most people.
 
• The country predominantly relied on **subsistence farming**, with farmers growing crops mainly for their consumption.
 
 
 
• **Impact of British Rule on Indian Agriculture:**
 
 
• The British focused heavily on **cash crops** like cotton, jute, and indigo for export, neglecting food crop production, which led to frequent famines.
 
• The **Zamindari system** introduced by the British exploited farmers, leading to financial hardships and poor agricultural practices.
 
 
 
• **Transition After Independence:**
 
 
• Post-independence, the government initiated measures like **land reforms**, the abolition of the Zamindari system, and the introduction of modern agricultural techniques to improve productivity.
 
• The **Green Revolution** in the 1960s further transformed the agricultural sector, making India self-sufficient in food production.
 
• Over time, the share of agriculture in the national income declined due to the rise of **industrialization** and the expansion of the service sector.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sectoral Contributions at Independence:**

 
 
• Agriculture contributed nearly **50%** to the national income.
 
• The **service sector** contributed a much smaller share as it was underdeveloped compared to agriculture.
 
• The **industrial sector** was highly underdeveloped due to colonial exploitation and lack of investment.
 
 
 
• **Current Scenario:**
 
 
• Today, the **services sector** is the largest contributor to India’s GDP, followed by industries and agriculture.
 
• Agriculture continues to play a vital role, employing a significant portion of India’s population, despite its reduced share in national income.

• Under this scheme, a subsidy is provided for **liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) connections**, making clean cooking fuel accessible to households that previously relied on traditional cooking methods like firewood and coal.
 
• This initiative targets women as the primary beneficiaries, considering their role in managing household cooking and the adverse health effects of using unclean fuels. *Hence, option 2 is correct.*

• The scheme also emphasizes **women empowerment** by easing their cooking burden and improving their quality of life, especially in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Specific Features of PMUY:**

 
 
• **Launch Date:** The scheme was launched on **May 1, 2016**, by the **Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi**.
 
• **Implementation:** It is implemented by the **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas**. Beneficiaries receive a financial support of **₹1,600** per connection.
 
• **Target Beneficiaries:** Women from families below the poverty line, including those belonging to **SC/ST communities, Most Backward Classes (MBC), and forest dwellers**.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of PMUY:**
 
 
• **Health Impact:** Reduction in exposure to harmful pollutants like **carbon monoxide (CO)** and **particulate matter (PM2.5)**, leading to better respiratory and cardiovascular health.
 
• **Environmental Impact:** Promotes the use of cleaner fuels, reducing deforestation and carbon emissions.
 
• **Economic Impact:** Saves time for women, enabling them to focus on education, work, or other activities.
 
 
 
• **Key Achievements:**
 
 
• Over **9 crore LPG connections** have been distributed under PMUY as of **2023**.
 
• The scheme has significantly contributed to increasing LPG penetration in rural areas, especially among economically backward households.

questions.question: During the colonial period in India, which social reformer worked for widow remarriage and against child marriage in Bengal?

__
 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**, a prominent social reformer during the colonial period in Bengal, is known for his relentless efforts to promote **widow remarriage** and oppose the practice of **child marriage**.
 
• He played a pivotal role in advocating the **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856**, which legalized widow remarriage in India, marking a significant milestone in social reform.
 
• Vidyasagar was deeply influenced by progressive ideas and sought to improve the status of women in society, challenging orthodox traditions that discriminated against widows. *Hence, statement is correct.*
 
• In addition to advocating widow remarriage, Vidyasagar campaigned against **child marriage**, highlighting its adverse effects on the physical and mental health of young girls.
 
• He was a staunch believer in **gender equality** and worked tirelessly to provide access to education for women, establishing several schools for girls. *Hence, statement is correct.*
 
• Vidyasagar's reformist actions were met with resistance from conservative elements of society, yet his efforts laid the foundation for progressive changes in Indian society.
 
• He was instrumental in shaping modern Bengali society and is remembered as a beacon of progress and social change in colonial India. *Hence, statement is correct.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856:**

 
 
• This act was a landmark legislation introduced during British rule in India. It was strongly advocated by **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** and passed on **July 26, 1856**.
 
• The act aimed to remove societal stigma surrounding widow remarriage and provide widows with legal and social recognition to remarry.
 
 
 
• **Opposition to Child Marriage:**
 
 
• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar actively campaigned against **child marriage**, which was widely practiced during the colonial period.
 
• He emphasized the adverse effects of child marriage on girls' health and sought to create awareness about its detrimental impact on society.
 
 
 
• **Contribution to Women's Education:**
 
 
• Vidyasagar was a pioneer in promoting **women's education** and founded several schools for girls in Bengal.
 
• He believed that **education** was the key to empowering women and enabling them to break free from societal constraints.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar:**

 
 
• He was born on **September 26, 1820**, in Bengal and is regarded as one of the greatest social reformers in Indian history.
 
• Vidyasagar was also a noted **educationist**, philosopher, and philanthropist, contributing significantly to the progress of Indian society.
 
 
 
• **Impact of His Reforms:**
 
 
• His efforts led to the passing of the **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act**, which was a turning point for women's rights in India.
 
• He laid the foundation for future social reform movements, inspiring several generations of reformers to work towards gender equality and human rights.

questions.question: Which resilient and adaptable polymer is frequently found in industrial brushes, toothbrushes, and other cleaning supplies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nylon 6, 6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nylon 6, 6** is a type of polyamide polymer known for its high tensile strength and resilience, making it ideal for industrial applications such as brushes, toothbrush bristles, and cleaning supplies.
 
• It is created by polymerizing **adipic acid and hexamethylene diamine**, forming strong molecular chains that give it excellent durability and adaptability.
 
• This polymer is highly resistant to wear, abrasion, and chemicals, making it suitable for applications requiring long-lasting performance. *Hence, statement is correct.*
 
• **Nylon 6, 6** has a high melting point and thermal stability, making it usable in environments involving heat or mechanical stress.
 
• Its flexibility allows it to be molded into various shapes, contributing to its widespread use in consumer and industrial products. *Hence, the correct answer is Nylon 6, 6.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Nylon 6, 6:**

 
 
• It is a synthetic polymer with **high tensile strength** and excellent elasticity, making it resistant to deformation under stress.
 
• Its **chemical resistance** allows it to withstand exposure to oils, solvents, and other chemicals, making it suitable for industrial environments.
 
• **Thermal properties:** Nylon 6, 6 has a melting point of approximately **260°C**, enabling its use in high-temperature applications.
 
• It exhibits **low friction** and good wear resistance, which makes it ideal for moving mechanical parts and cleaning tools.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Nylon 6, 6:**
 
 
• It is extensively used in manufacturing **industrial brushes, toothbrush bristles, machine parts, fabrics, and fishing lines**.
 
• In the automotive industry, it is used for **engine components, fuel lines, and other durable parts**.
 
• In construction, Nylon 6, 6 is utilized for **ropes and nets** due to its strength and resistance to environmental factors.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Neoprene:** A synthetic rubber used for weather-resistant applications, wetsuits, and seals. It lacks the durability and adaptability of Nylon 6, 6.
 
• **Terylene:** A polyester polymer primarily used in textiles, but it does not possess the same mechanical resilience as Nylon 6, 6.
 
• **Teflon:** Known for its non-stick properties, Teflon is used in cookware and coatings but is not suitable for bristles or brushes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **History of Nylon:**

 
 
• **Invented in 1935** by Wallace Carothers at **DuPont**, Nylon revolutionized the synthetic polymer industry.
 
• Initially used in **textile manufacturing**, it later found applications in industrial and consumer products due to its versatility.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Considerations:**
 
 
• Nylon production involves petrochemical processes, raising concerns about sustainability and environmental impact.
 
• Efforts are underway to develop **biodegradable alternatives** to reduce ecological footprints.

questions.question: A significant river of the Indian Desert, Luni originates from western slopes of the Aravalli ranges near which place in Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ajmer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Luni River** is a significant river flowing through the arid region of the Indian desert in Rajasthan.
 
• The river originates from the **western slopes of the Aravalli ranges**, near the town of **Ajmer** in Rajasthan.
 
• Ajmer is located in the central part of Rajasthan and is surrounded by the Aravalli hills, making it a suitable geographical location for river origins. *Hence, the correct option is Ajmer.*
 
• The Luni River flows southwest and drains into the **Rann of Kutch**, making it one of the few rivers in India that flows into an inland basin rather than the sea.
 
• Its name "Luni" is derived from its saline water, which is a result of the high salt content in the region. *This further highlights the uniqueness of the river.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Importance of Ajmer:**

 
 
• Ajmer is located in the **central part of Rajasthan**, surrounded by the **Aravalli ranges**, which play a significant role in the origin of rivers like Luni.
 
• The region has a semi-arid climate, and rivers originating here often have saline water due to the geological characteristics of the area.
 
 
 
• **About the Luni River:**
 
 
• The Luni River is considered a vital water source for irrigation in the **Indian desert region**, despite its saline water.
 
• It originates near Ajmer and flows through districts like **Pali, Jodhpur, Barmer, and Jalore**.
 
• The river finally ends in the **Rann of Kutch**, which is a salt marsh located in Gujarat.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Udaipur:** Known as the "City of Lakes," Udaipur is located in southern Rajasthan and is famous for its picturesque lakes rather than being a source of the Luni River.
 
• **Rajsamand:** It is famous for the Rajsamand Lake and does not serve as the origin point for the Luni River.
 
• **Sirohi:** Located in the south-western region of Rajasthan, Sirohi is known for Mount Abu but is not related to the Luni River's origin.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the Aravalli Ranges:**

 
 
• The **Aravalli ranges** are one of the oldest mountain ranges in India, stretching across Rajasthan, Haryana, and Gujarat.
 
• They play an essential role in influencing the climatic and hydrological patterns of the region, including the origin of rivers like Luni.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance of Luni River:**
 
 
• Even though the river water is saline, it is extensively used for **irrigation** in the desert region.
 
• The river supports agriculture and livestock, making it a critical resource for the arid and semi-arid zones of Rajasthan.

questions.question: Which stone was mainly utilised in building the Chennakeshava Temple in Belur, India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Soapstone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Soapstone**, also known as steatite, was the primary material used in constructing the **Chennakeshava Temple** in **Belur, Karnataka**, India.
 
• This material is widely appreciated for its **softness**, which makes it easy to carve intricate designs and sculptures, a hallmark of the **Hoysala architecture**.
 
• The temple, built during the **Hoysala Empire** in the 12th century, showcases elaborate carvings and fine details that are made possible due to the **workability of soapstone**. *Hence, Soapstone is the correct answer.*
 
• **Soapstone** is also durable and resistant to weathering, making it suitable for long-lasting structures like temples.
 
• The intricate carvings, such as depictions of deities, dancers, and cultural motifs, are made easier by the softness of soapstone, which can be finely detailed by skilled artisans. *Hence, the correct material for the Chennakeshava Temple is Soapstone.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Soapstone:**

 
 
• **Soapstone** is a metamorphic rock composed mainly of talc and magnesium silicate. It is soft, easy to carve, and has been used historically for sculptures and architecture.
 
• It is durable and weather-resistant, making it a popular choice for constructing temples and other monuments that require intricate detailing.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The **Chennakeshava Temple** was commissioned by King Vishnuvardhana of the Hoysala Empire in **1117 CE**.
 
• The temple is dedicated to Lord Vishnu and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site nominee due to its architectural brilliance and historical significance.
 
• **Hoysala architecture** is characterized by its star-shaped platforms, intricate carvings, and detailed sculptures, all of which were achieved using **soapstone**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Materials:**
 
 
• **Marble:** Although marble is also used for intricate carvings and sculptures, it is harder than soapstone and was not commonly used in Hoysala architecture.
 
• **Sandstone:** Sandstone is harder and more commonly used in North Indian temples like those in Rajasthan but lacks the softness required for intricate carvings.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of subsistence farming?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Farming for family consumption**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Subsistence farming** is primarily aimed at **meeting the needs of the farmer's family**. The crops produced are consumed by the family, with little to no surplus left for sale in the market.
 
• This type of farming is common in **developing countries**, where farmers rely on traditional techniques and tools for cultivation.
 
• The focus of subsistence farming is on **basic staple crops**, such as rice, wheat, maize, and millet, which are essential for the farmer's household consumption.
 
• Unlike commercial farming, subsistence farming does **not emphasize profit-making**. It is a small-scale activity centered on the survival of the family. Hence, farming for family consumption is the correct answer.
 
• Options like "Use of modern irrigation techniques" and "Use of high-yielding varieties" are incorrect as these are usually associated with **modern or commercial farming** rather than subsistence farming.
 
• Similarly, "Commercial crop production" is not a characteristic of subsistence farming. Instead, it focuses on producing crops for **market sale** and profit, which differs from the goal of subsistence farming. Thus, these options are not correct.
 
• Subsistence farming is often practiced in **rural areas** with limited resources, where farmers depend on natural rainfall and organic fertilizers.
 
• This type of farming is labor-intensive and involves the use of simple tools like plows, hoes, and sickles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Features of Subsistence Farming:**

 
 
• **Small Land Holdings:** The land used for cultivation is usually small and is worked on by the family members themselves.
 
• **Traditional Methods:** Farmers rely on traditional farming methods, such as manual plowing and organic fertilizers.
 
• **Rain-fed Irrigation:** Most subsistence farming is dependent on natural rainfall rather than advanced irrigation systems.
 
• **Low Productivity:** Due to the lack of modern techniques and resources, the productivity of subsistence farming is relatively low.
 
 
 
• **Prevalence of Subsistence Farming:**
 
 
• **Developing Countries:** Subsistence farming is widely practiced in countries such as **India, Nepal, Bangladesh, and many African nations**, where agriculture is the primary source of livelihood for many families.
 
• **Remote Areas:** It is more common in rural and remote regions with limited access to markets, resources, and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Commercial Farming:**
 
 
• **Objective:** While subsistence farming focuses on survival, commercial farming aims at generating profit.
 
• **Use of Technology:** Modern machinery and advanced techniques are typically used in commercial farming, unlike subsistence farming.
 
• **Market Orientation:** In commercial farming, crops are grown for sale, while in subsistence farming, they are primarily for family consumption.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Types of Subsistence Farming:**

 
 
• **Primitive Subsistence Farming:** Practiced in small patches of land using primitive tools. Examples include shifting cultivation and nomadic herding.
 
• **Intensive Subsistence Farming:** Characterized by the use of more labor and simple tools to produce maximum yield on small land areas. It is commonly seen in densely populated regions of **Asia**.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Subsistence Farming:**
 
 
• **Climate Dependency:** Farmers are heavily reliant on weather conditions, making them vulnerable to droughts or floods.
 
• **Lack of Modern Inputs:** Limited access to fertilizers, quality seeds, and irrigation facilities reduces productivity.

questions.question: The Nizam of Hyderabad accepted British subsidiary alliance under ________________.

__
 
• The **Subsidiary Alliance** was a policy introduced by **Lord Wellesley**, who served as the Governor-General of India from **1798 to 1805**. This policy was aimed at extending British control over the Indian princely states.
 
• The main feature of this policy was that the Indian rulers had to accept British forces to be stationed within their territories and pay for their maintenance. In return, they would receive protection from external threats and internal revolts.
 
• The **Nizam of Hyderabad** was the first Indian ruler to accept the Subsidiary Alliance in **1798**. This made Hyderabad a dependent ally of the British Empire, and the Nizam ceded control over his foreign relations to the British. *Hence, the correct answer is Lord Wellesley.*
 
• The acceptance of the alliance by the Nizam marked a significant milestone in British expansionism in India, as it allowed them to establish a firm foothold in southern India. This was also a strategic move to counter threats from other powers like the French.
 
• Under the terms of the Subsidiary Alliance, the Nizam agreed to disband his existing army and rely solely on the British forces for protection. This severely limited his sovereignty and made Hyderabad a satellite state of the British Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Subsidiary Alliance:**

 
 
• This was a diplomatic strategy by **Lord Wellesley** to expand British influence in India without direct annexation. It enabled the British to control the foreign policies of Indian rulers while reducing their military capabilities.
 
• Under this alliance, Indian rulers were required to station British troops in their territories and pay for their upkeep. Failure to pay would result in the cession of territory.
 
• **Example:** Apart from Hyderabad, other states like Mysore, Tanjore, and Awadh also accepted the Subsidiary Alliance.
 
 
 
• **Lord Wellesley:**
 
 
• He was the **Governor-General of India** from **1798 to 1805**. Known for his aggressive expansionist policies, he aimed to establish British supremacy in India through treaties and alliances.
 
• The Subsidiary Alliance was one of his most significant policies, which allowed the British to exercise indirect control over Indian states.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Subsidiary Alliance:**
 
 
• It increased British control and influence in India. However, it weakened the Indian rulers militarily and financially, making them dependent on the British.
 
• It paved the way for further annexations and the eventual establishment of British rule over most of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of Subsidiary Alliance:**

 
 
• The Indian ruler had to disband his own army and rely on British troops for protection.
 
• The ruler had to pay for the maintenance of British troops, failing which territory would be ceded as payment.
 
• The ruler could not employ any European in his service without British approval.
 
• The ruler had to accept a British Resident in his court, who would oversee the administration and act as a representative of British interests.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Subsidiary Alliance was part of the British strategy to counter the influence of other European powers, particularly the French, in India during the late 18th and early 19th centuries.
 
• It played a key role in the expansion of British territories and influence in India, paving the way for the establishment of the British Empire.

questions.question: If an object moves up to four times faster than the speed of sound, the condition is called:

• The condition where an object moves up to f**our times faster** than the speed of sound is called **supersonic **speed.
 
• This speed is also often expressed as a Mach number of up to Mach 4, where **Mach 1 is the speed of sound. **
 
• **Supersonic **refers to conditions where an object travels at a speed between **Mach 1 to Mach 5**.
 
• The speed of sound in air is approximately **343 meters per second****.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Categories of Speed:**

 
 
• **Subsonic:** Speeds lower than the speed of sound (below Mach 1). Examples include commercial airplanes such as the **Boeing 737**.
 
• **Transonic:** Speeds close to the speed of sound (Mach 0.8–1.2). This range includes aircraft transitioning through the speed of sound, where air pressure changes significantly.
 
• **Supersonic:** Speeds greater than the speed of sound (Mach 1–5). Examples include military jets like the **F-22 Raptor**.
 
• **Hypersonic:** Speeds exceeding Mach 5. This is the realm of cutting-edge technology like **space shuttles and hypersonic missiles**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Hypersonic Technology:**
 
 
• **Military:** Hypersonic missiles are being developed by countries like **Russia, the United States, and China** for rapid, precise strikes.

• Complex propulsion systems, such as **scramjets**, are required to maintain hypersonic speeds.

• **Scientific Advances:**

• Hypersonic vehicles have significant potential in the fields of **space exploration**, defense, and commercial transportation, allowing for faster global travel.
 
 
 
• **Historical Development:**
 
 
• The first hypersonic flight was achieved by the **X-15 rocket plane**, which reached speeds of Mach 6.72 in **1967**.
 
• **Current developments** include the U.S. Air Force's **Hypersonic Conventional Strike Weapon (HCSW)** program and Russia's **Avangard hypersonic missile.**

questions.question: According to the Brønsted-Lowry theory, which of the following defines an acid?
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**Donates a proton**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • According to the **Brønsted-Lowry theory**, an acid is defined as a substance that **donates a proton (H⁺ ion)** to another substance. This makes option 1 correct. • The theory was proposed by **Johannes Nicolaus Brønsted** and **Thomas Martin Lowry** in 1923 to explain the behavior of acids and bases in terms of proton transfer. • Option 2, "Donates a hydroxide ion," is incorrect because hydroxide ions (OH⁻) are associated with bases, not acids. • Option 3, "Accepts a proton," is incorrect because accepting a proton is the property of a **Brønsted-Lowry base**, not an acid. • Option 4, "Accepts an electron pair," is not applicable under the Brønsted-Lowry theory. Instead, this is a characteristic of **Lewis acids**, which accept electron pairs. • The Brønsted-Lowry theory specifically focuses on the transfer of protons (H⁺ ions) between substances, making option 1 the most accurate definition of an acid in this context. • Therefore, the correct answer is **Donates a proton**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __ • **Brønsted-Lowry Theory:** • The Brønsted-Lowry theory defines acids as substances that **donate protons** (H⁺ ions) and bases as substances that **accept protons**. • The proton transfer process occurs in aqueous solutions, where acids release protons and bases capture them. • Examples of Brønsted-Lowry acids include **HCl** (hydrochloric acid), which donates a proton to water, forming hydronium ions (H₃O⁺). • **Comparison with Other Theories:** • **Arrhenius Theory:** Defines acids as substances that increase the concentration of H⁺ ions in an aqueous solution and bases as substances that increase OH⁻ concentration. • **Lewis Theory:** Defines acids as electron-pair acceptors and bases as electron-pair donors. This is a broader theory compared to the Brønsted-Lowry definition. • **Examples of Brønsted-Lowry Acids and Bases:** • **Acids:** HCl, H₂SO₄, HNO₃, CH₃COOH (acetic acid). • **Bases:** NH₃ (ammonia), OH⁻ (hydroxide ion), and CO₃²⁻ (carbonate ion). [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** • **Applications of the Brønsted-Lowry Theory:** • The theory is widely used in chemistry to explain **acid-base reactions**, such as neutralization reactions where acids and bases react to form water and a salt. • It helps in understanding the behavior of compounds in water and other solvents, especially in titration and buffer systems. • **Limitations of the Theory:** • The Brønsted-Lowry theory is limited to proton transfer and does not explain acid-base behavior in non-aqueous systems where no protons are involved. • For example, it cannot explain the behavior of substances like BF₃ (boron trifluoride), which act as acids by accepting electron pairs but do not donate protons. f3:T2bf4,

questions.question: The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) was a result of which global conference?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earth Summit, 1992**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)** was adopted during the **Earth Summit**, which was held in **Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in 1992**.
 
• The **Earth Summit**, officially known as the **United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (UNCED)**, was a landmark global conference that focused on sustainable development and environmental protection.
 
• The CBD is an international treaty aimed at **conserving biodiversity**, promoting **sustainable use** of its components, and ensuring the **fair and equitable sharing of benefits** arising from the utilization of genetic resources.
 
• It was one of the key outcomes of the Earth Summit, alongside other agreements like the **Agenda 21**, the **Rio Declaration**, and the **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)**.
 
• The CBD entered into force on **December 29, 1993**, and has been ratified by nearly all countries worldwide. *Hence, the statement is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Earth Summit, 1992:**

 
 
• The **Earth Summit** was held from **June 3 to June 14, 1992**, in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, and was attended by **over 100 heads of state** and representatives from 178 nations.
 
• Its goal was to address urgent environmental and development issues such as **deforestation, climate change, loss of biodiversity, and sustainable development**.
 
• The summit led to the creation of several key international agreements, including the **CBD**, **UNFCCC**, and the **United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD)**.
 
 
 
• **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD):**
 
 
• The CBD aims to **conserve biodiversity**, promote its **sustainable use**, and ensure the **fair sharing of benefits** from genetic resources.
 
• It covers ecosystems, species, and genetic resources and emphasizes the importance of protecting traditional knowledge and practices related to biodiversity.
 
• The CBD has three main objectives: **conservation of biological diversity**, sustainable use of its components, and **equitable sharing of benefits** arising from genetic resources.
 
 
 
• **Other Conferences Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Stockholm Conference (1972):** Known as the United Nations Conference on the Human Environment, it was the first major international meeting on environmental issues. It led to the establishment of the United Nations Environment Programme (**UNEP**).
 
• **Paris Agreement (2015):** An international treaty within the **UNFCCC**, focused on limiting global warming to below 2 degrees Celsius.
 
• **Kyoto Conference (1997):** Adopted the **Kyoto Protocol**, an international treaty that committed industrialized countries to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Facts about the CBD:**

 
 
• As of **October 2023**, the CBD has been ratified by **196 parties**, including nearly every country except the **United States**.
 
• The CBD has inspired several protocols, such as the **Cartagena Protocol** on Biosafety (2003) and the **Nagoya Protocol** on Access and Benefit Sharing (2014).
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Earth Summit:**
 
 
• The summit marked the beginning of global cooperation on environmental issues and sustainable development.
 
• It highlighted the **interdependence** of economic development and environmental preservation.

questions.question: In May 2025, ISRO's Aditya-L1 mission released its first set of scientific data. What is the primary objective of this mission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Observe the Sun's outermost layer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aditya-L1 Mission:** The **Aditya-L1 mission** is India’s first dedicated solar mission, developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**. Its primary objective is to study the **Sun's outermost layer**, known as the **corona**, and understand solar phenomena.
 
• **Lagrange Point 1:** The spacecraft is stationed in a **halo orbit around the Lagrange Point 1 (L1)**, which is approximately **1.5 million kilometers** from Earth. This position provides a continuous view of the Sun without the interference of eclipses or occultation.
 
• **Scientific Goals:** The mission aims to study **solar wind**, **solar radiation**, and **magnetic field dynamics**, providing crucial insights into the behavior of space weather and its impact on Earth.
 
• **Instruments:** Aditya-L1 is equipped with **seven payloads**, including the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) and Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (SUIT), to observe the Sun's atmosphere and its dynamics.
 
• **Importance:** By studying the Sun, ISRO’s Aditya-L1 mission contributes to global efforts in understanding **solar energy, space weather, and solar storms**, which have the potential to affect satellites, communication systems, and power grids.
 
• ***Hence, the correct objective of the Aditya-L1 mission is to "Observe the Sun's outermost layer."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aditya-L1 Mission Details:**

 
 
• Aditya-L1 was launched by ISRO aboard the **PSLV-C57** in **September 2023**. It is named after the Sun god **Aditya** in Indian mythology.
 
• The spacecraft is equipped with instruments such as the **VELC**, **SUIT**, **Solar Low Energy X-ray Spectrometer (SoLEXS)**, and others to observe the Sun's corona, chromosphere, and photosphere.
 
 
 
• **Lagrange Point 1 (L1):**
 
 
• L1 is a position in space where the gravitational forces of the Earth and the Sun balance the orbital motion of a satellite. Aditya-L1’s placement here allows uninterrupted observations of the Sun.
 
• This strategic location enables the spacecraft to collect real-time data on solar activities, such as solar flares and coronal mass ejections, which are crucial for studying space weather.
 
 
 
• **Impacts of Solar Studies:**
 
 
• Understanding solar phenomena helps predict **geomagnetic storms** and their effects on Earth. These storms can disrupt satellite communications, navigation systems, and even power grids.
 
• The research will also assist in improving space weather models, ensuring better preparedness for potential disruptions caused by solar activities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Missions for Comparison:**

 
 
• **Mars Orbiter Mission:** India’s first interplanetary mission launched in **2013** aimed to study **Mars’ atmosphere**, not the Sun.
 
• **Chandrayaan Missions:** These missions focus on lunar exploration, including studying the **Moon's surface** and water presence.
 
• **Deep Space Missions:** Missions like NASA’s Voyager and ISRO’s planned Shukrayaan focus on exploring **deep space phenomena**, rather than the Sun.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Aditya-L1:**
 
 
• Aditya-L1 is a landmark for India’s space program as it marks the nation’s first attempt to study the Sun directly and contribute to global solar research.
 
• The mission is expected to provide valuable data for understanding the Sun’s influence on the Earth and its environment.

questions.question: Which type of memory loses all its stored data when the power is turned off?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RAM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory)** is a type of **volatile memory**, meaning it loses all stored data when the power is turned off. This is because RAM is designed to store data temporarily for immediate access by the processor.
 
• RAM is used to store data and instructions that are actively being used or processed by the computer. Once the system is powered down, all data stored in RAM is erased.*Hence, RAM loses data when power is turned off.*
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)**, in contrast, is a type of **non-volatile memory**, meaning data stored within ROM remains intact even when the system is powered off. *Hence, ROM does not lose data when power is turned off.*
 
• **USB flash drives** and **hard disk drives** are also examples of non-volatile storage devices. They retain data regardless of the power state of the device.*Hence, neither USB flash drives nor hard disk drives lose data when power is turned off.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of RAM:**

 
 
• **Volatile Memory:** RAM requires continuous power to maintain its data. When the power supply is interrupted, all data stored in RAM is lost.
 
• **Speed:** RAM is significantly faster than other types of storage like hard drives or SSDs, making it ideal for temporary storage of active processes.
 
• **Types:** Common types of RAM include **DRAM (Dynamic RAM)** and **SRAM (Static RAM)**. DRAM is widely used for main memory, while SRAM is used for cache memory due to its faster speed.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of ROM:**
 
 
• **Non-Volatile Memory:** ROM retains its data even when the system is powered off. It is used to store critical data such as firmware.
 
• **Usage:** ROM is commonly used in embedded systems and devices to store software that needs to persist across power cycles, such as the BIOS in computers.
 
 
 
• **USB Flash Drive:**
 
 
• **Portable Storage:** USB flash drives are non-volatile storage devices used to transfer data between systems or store files externally.
 
• **Durability:** Data remains intact even after the device is removed or the power is turned off.
 
 
 
• **Hard Disk Drive (HDD):**
 
 
• **Non-Volatile Memory:** HDDs are used for long-term storage of data. Data remains intact even when the computer is powered off.
 
• **Storage Capacity:** HDDs provide large storage capacity for personal and enterprise use compared to RAM.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison of RAM and ROM:**

 
 
• **RAM:** Volatile memory used for temporary storage of active processes. Data is lost when power is turned off.
 
• **ROM:** Non-volatile memory used for permanent storage of critical data. Data is retained even when power is turned off.
 
 
 
• **Applications of RAM and ROM:**
 
 
• **RAM:** Used in computers, laptops, and smartphones to manage active processes and tasks.
 
• **ROM:** Used in embedded systems, firmware storage, and devices requiring persistent software.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Storage Devices:**
 
 
• **USB Flash Drives:** Portable non-volatile storage devices introduced in the early 2000s.
 
• **HDD:** Mechanical storage devices that have been widely used since the mid-20th century for long-term data storage.

questions.question: What is the main reason behind the formation of lagoons along the Eastern Coastal Plains?

options.text: Sand deposition along the shallow coastlines
Tectonic activity and fault line shifts
Coral reef development and volcanic islands
Deposition by rivers and wave action along the coast

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deposition by rivers and wave action along the coast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lagoons** are shallow water bodies separated from the main sea by sandbars, barrier islands, or coral reefs. They are commonly found along the **Eastern Coastal Plains of India**.
 
• The Eastern Coastal Plains are characterized by their **low-lying terrain**, which facilitates the accumulation of sediments brought by rivers and waves.
 
• The process of **deposition by rivers** involves the movement of sediments like sand and silt from rivers into the coastal areas, which eventually creates sandbars and barriers that form lagoons. *Hence, the correct explanation is deposition by rivers and wave action.*
 
• **Wave action** plays a crucial role in forming lagoons. Waves deposit sediments along the coastline, creating a barrier between the lagoon and the open sea.
 
• Additionally, lagoons along the eastern coast are more prominent due to the **nature of the coastline**, which is relatively flat and conducive to sediment accumulation. *Hence, the statement explaining deposition by rivers and wave action is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Formation of Lagoons:**

 
 
• **Wave action:** Lagoons are formed when waves deposit sand and other sediments along the coast, creating barriers that isolate small water bodies.
 
• **River deposition:** Rivers often carry sediments like sand and silt from their upper courses to the coastal areas. These sediments accumulate over time, forming sandbars that create lagoons.
 
• **Geographical features:** Lagoons are typically found in coastal regions with flat terrain and shallow coastlines, as seen along the Eastern Coastal Plains of India.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Eastern Coastal Plains:**
 
 
• The Eastern Coastal Plains of India are broader and more fertile compared to the Western Coastal Plains. They extend along the Bay of Bengal.
 
• **Examples:** Well-known lagoons in India include the **Chilika Lake** in Odisha, which is one of the largest lagoons in the world.
 
 
 
• **Other factors influencing lagoon formation:**
 
 
• **Tides:** Tidal activities play a role in maintaining the water flow in lagoons.
 
• **Human intervention:** In some areas, human activities like the construction of dams or embankments have also contributed to the formation of lagoons.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Examples of Lagoons in India:**

 
 
• **Chilika Lake:** Located in Odisha, it is the largest coastal lagoon in India and a vital ecosystem supporting diverse flora and fauna.
 
• **Pulicat Lake:** Situated on the border of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, it is another significant lagoon formed due to deposition by rivers and wave action.

questions.question: Which of the following is INCORRECT about the Harappans?

options.text: The most favoured ornaments were beads of carnelian.
They exported ornaments, timber, some objects of daily use.
The Harappans were engaged in active trade.
The Harappans used only gold to make tools, pots and pans.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Harappans were skilled artisans**, particularly in crafting ornaments using materials like **carnelian, lapis lazuli, gold, silver, and other semiprecious stones**. Beads made of carnelian were among the most favoured ornaments. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• The Harappans engaged in **active trade**. They exported **ornaments, timber, and various objects of daily use**, and imported goods like gold, copper, and other raw materials for their industries. This indicates a well-established trade network. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.*
 
• Trade was an integral part of Harappan society, as evident from the discovery of seals, weights, and other trade-related artifacts. Their trade extended to Mesopotamia and other contemporary civilizations. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• The statement that the Harappans used only **gold to make tools, pots, and pans** is incorrect. The Harappans were known to use copper, bronze, and stone for making tools and utensils. Gold was primarily reserved for ornaments and jewelry due to its value and soft nature, which made it unsuitable for crafting tools or utilitarian items. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
• ***Thus, the correct answer is Option 4.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Overview of the Harappan Civilization:**

 
 
• The **Harappan Civilization**, also known as the **Indus Valley Civilization**, flourished between approximately **3300 BCE and 1300 BCE**.
 
• It spanned modern-day **Pakistan**, **India**, and parts of **Afghanistan**, covering an area of about 1.25 million square kilometers.
 
• The civilization was characterized by advanced urban planning, including the use of **grid layouts**, drainage systems, and granaries.
 
 
 
• **Trade and Economy:**
 
 
• The Harappans traded with **Mesopotamia, Central Asia, and other neighboring regions**. Trade items included textiles, beads, pottery, and semi-precious stones.
 
• **Artifacts like seals and weights** indicate a standardized system for trade and commerce.
 
• They imported **raw materials** such as lapis lazuli from Afghanistan, copper from Rajasthan and Oman, and timber from the Himalayas.
 
 
 
• **Tools and Materials Used by Harappans:**
 
 
• The Harappans primarily used **copper, bronze, and stone** for crafting tools, weapons, and utensils.
 
• Gold was reserved for making ornaments like necklaces, rings, and other decorative items.
 
• Other materials like **terracotta** and shell were used to create figurines and ornaments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Carnelian:**

 
 
• **Carnelian**, a reddish-brown semi-precious stone, was one of the most popular materials for crafting beads and ornaments in the Harappan civilization.
 
• It was often polished and shaped using advanced techniques to create intricate designs.
 
 
 
• **Urban Planning:**
 
 
• The Harappan cities, such as **Harappa** and **Mohenjo-Daro**, showcased remarkable urban planning with well-organized streets, brick houses, and drainage systems.
 
• These features reflected a high level of engineering and architectural expertise.
 
 
 
• **Use of Gold:**
 
 
• Gold was primarily used for **decorative purposes** and not for practical tools or utensils due to its softness.
 
• Examples include **gold jewelry** excavated from various Harappan sites, indicating its use for aesthetic purposes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a shallow desert depression formed by wind erosion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deflation hollow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Deflation hollows** are shallow depressions formed in desert landscapes due to **wind erosion**. Strong winds remove loose particles from the surface, creating depressions over time.
 
• These hollows are typically found in arid or semi-arid regions where the wind has sufficient force to erode and carry away fine particles such as sand and silt.
 
• The process of deflation, which refers to the removal of fine soil and sediment by wind, is responsible for the formation of these hollows. *Hence, the term "deflation hollow" is appropriate for this feature.*
 
• Deflation hollows vary in size, ranging from small pits to large depressions that can span several kilometers.
 
• The most significant examples of deflation hollows are found in regions like the **Sahara Desert** and the **Kalahari Desert**, where strong winds persist over time. *Hence, the correct answer is Deflation hollow.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pediment:**

 
 
• A pediment is a **gentle slope or broad, flat area** typically found at the base of mountains or hills. It is formed by erosion and deposition, not specifically wind erosion.
 
• Pediments are generally covered with **alluvial deposits** and are not considered shallow depressions. Hence, this is not the correct answer.
 
 
 
• **Playa:**
 
 
• A playa is a **dry lake bed** found in desert areas. It forms when water evaporates, leaving behind salt, clay, and other sediments.
 
• Unlike deflation hollows, playas are generally **flat and expansive**, and their formation is more related to evaporation rather than wind erosion. Hence, this is not the correct answer.
 
 
 
• **Inselberg:**
 
 
• An inselberg is an isolated hill or mountain that rises abruptly from a plain. It is formed due to the weathering and erosion of surrounding rock, leaving behind resistant rock.
 
• Inselbergs are solid rock formations and do not resemble shallow depressions. Examples include **Uluru** in Australia. Hence, this is not the correct answer.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Deflation Hollow Characteristics:**

 
 
• The size of deflation hollows depends on the **intensity and duration of wind activity**. Stronger winds lead to the formation of larger hollows.
 
• Deflation hollows are often found in areas with **loose, unconsolidated sediments**, such as sand or silt.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Deflation Hollows:**
 
 
• The **Qattara Depression** in Egypt is one of the largest deflation hollows in the world, spanning over 18,000 square kilometers.
 
• Other notable examples include the **Turpan Depression** in China and various hollows in the deserts of North America.

questions.question: Privatisation aims to improve _____ in public enterprises.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**operational efficiency and competitiveness**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Privatisation** refers to the transfer of ownership, management, and control of public enterprises to private entities. Its main goal is to improve the **operational efficiency** and make enterprises more competitive in the market.
 
• **Operational efficiency** increases because private entities focus on cost reduction, profit maximization, and resource optimization, which leads to better productivity and service delivery.
 
• Privatisation reduces bureaucratic control and political influence in decision-making processes. Private management tends to prioritize business goals over political or administrative considerations. *Hence, statement 3 and 4 are not the primary aims.*
 
• **Competitiveness** is enhanced as privatized enterprises need to compete in the market, encouraging innovation, customer satisfaction, and better quality of products or services.
 
• Privatisation also reduces **government expenditure** as the financial burden of maintaining public enterprises shifts to private entities, allowing the government to focus resources on other sectors. *However, improving government expenditure is not the primary aim.*
 
• The above reasons make the correct answer **operational efficiency and competitiveness**, which are the core objectives of privatisation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Privatisation:**

 
 
• **Privatisation** can be implemented through various methods such as **disinvestment**, outright sale, public-private partnerships (**PPP**), and outsourcing.
 
• It aims to bring in private capital, expertise, and management practices to improve efficiency and competitiveness in sectors such as **transport, energy, banking**, and manufacturing.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Privatisation:**
 
 
• Increased **efficiency:** Private enterprises typically operate with a goal to maximize profits, which drives operational efficiency and innovation.
 
• **Competitiveness:** It fosters competition, leading to better products and services for consumers.
 
• Reduces **financial burden:** The government can allocate funds to crucial areas such as education, healthcare, and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Disadvantages of Privatisation:**
 
 
• **Social inequality:** Privatised enterprises may prioritize profit over social welfare, leading to disparities in access to essential services.
 
• **Job insecurity:** Privatisation often leads to workforce downsizing as private entities aim to reduce operational costs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Examples of Privatisation:**

 
 
• The **disinvestment** of companies such as **Air India** and **Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL)** are examples of privatisation in India.
 
• **Privatisation of Indian Railways:** Initiatives like private trains such as **Tejas Express** are steps towards introducing private players in rail transportation.
 
 
 
• **Global Examples:**
 
 
• In the **United Kingdom**, privatisation efforts include the sale of British Telecom, British Airways, and British Gas under Margaret Thatcher.
 
• **Privatisation in the United States:** The US has privatized sectors like **telecommunications, railways, and energy**, leading to improved market dynamics.

questions.question: Which of the following communities may apply for Indian citizenship after just 6 years of residence, as per the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikhs from Pakistan**__.

__
 
• The **Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019** provides expedited citizenship for members of specific religious communities persecuted in neighboring countries such as **Pakistan, Afghanistan, and Bangladesh**.
 
• The Act reduced the residency requirement for citizenship from **12 years to 6 years** for certain groups. These groups include **Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, and Christians** fleeing religious persecution in the aforementioned countries.
 
• It specifically mentions communities such as **Sikhs from Pakistan**, Hindus from Bangladesh, Buddhists from Afghanistan, etc., as eligible for accelerated citizenship. *Hence, Sikhs from Pakistan are eligible.*
 
• The Act does not cover Jews from Israel or Buddhists from Nepal, as it focuses on religious minorities persecuted in specific neighboring countries. *Hence, statements regarding Buddhists from Nepal and Jews from Israel are incorrect.*
 
• Similarly, Hindus from Sri Lanka do not fall under the purview of this Act, as Sri Lanka is not one of the countries mentioned in the Act. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Sikhs from Pakistan.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019:**

 
 
• This Act amends the **Citizenship Act, 1955** to allow members of certain persecuted religious communities from Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Afghanistan to obtain citizenship faster.
 
• It applies to **Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, and Christians** who entered India before **31st December 2014** due to religious persecution.
 
 
 
• **Key Provisions:**
 
 
• The Act reduces the residency requirement for citizenship via naturalization from **12 years to 6 years** for eligible communities.
 
• It excludes certain areas such as **tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram, and Tripura**, as well as areas under the Sixth Schedule and states protected by the **Inner Line Permit (ILP)**.
 
 
 
• **Exclusions from the Act:**
 
 
• The Act does not cover **Muslims** from Pakistan, Bangladesh, or Afghanistan, as the focus is on religious minorities facing persecution in these countries.
 
• It also does not apply to refugees from other countries like **Myanmar, Sri Lanka, or Nepal**.
 
• The Act has sparked debates and protests regarding its constitutionality and alleged discrimination based on religion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Challenges:**

 
 
• The Act has faced criticism for allegedly violating the **secular principles** enshrined in the **Indian Constitution**. Critics argue that it excludes Muslims and focuses solely on specific religious groups.
 
• Supporters of the Act argue that it provides much-needed relief to minorities fleeing persecution and aligns with India's historic role as a refuge for oppressed communities.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• India has historically provided asylum to persecuted communities, such as the **Parsis fleeing Iran** and **Tibetan Buddhists** escaping Chinese oppression.
 
• The **Partition of India in 1947** led to mass migrations and significant challenges for religious minorities in Pakistan and Bangladesh.
 
• The Act seeks to address these historical injustices faced by religious minorities in neighboring countries.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of soft infrastructure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Public education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Soft infrastructure** refers to the institutions, services, and frameworks that support the functioning of a society and economy. These elements often focus on human capital and social systems rather than physical structures.
 
• **Public education** is an example of soft infrastructure because it involves systems and institutions that deliver educational services, contributing to the development of human capital. It fosters intellectual growth, skill development, and social cohesion among citizens.
 
• Soft infrastructure includes aspects like **healthcare systems, financial frameworks, governance mechanisms**, and educational institutions. *Hence, the correct answer is Public education.*
 
• Options such as **water pipelines, bridges, and airports** represent examples of **hard infrastructure**. Hard infrastructure refers to the physical systems required for the operation of a society, like transportation, energy, and water supply.
 
• While hard infrastructure focuses on tangible assets, soft infrastructure ensures the seamless functioning of societal frameworks. Public education builds the knowledge base and skill sets essential for societal progress. *Hence, the correct answer is Public education.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Soft Infrastructure:**

 
 
• **Soft infrastructure** encompasses the services, programs, and institutions that support societal and economic functioning. Examples include **education systems, healthcare frameworks, law enforcement bodies, and governance mechanisms.**
 
• Unlike hard infrastructure, soft infrastructure builds **intellectual, social, and economic capital**. It focuses on intangible assets that underpin the functioning of a nation.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Hard Infrastructure:**
 
 
• Hard infrastructure refers to physical assets like **roads, bridges, railways, airports, and pipelines.**
 
• It provides the backbone for transportation, energy, communication, and water supply systems, ensuring the physical connectivity and operational efficiency of a society.
 
• **Example:** Bridges facilitate the movement of goods and people, while water pipelines ensure the distribution of water resources.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Public Education:**
 
 
• **Public education** contributes to the development of human capital, which is vital for economic growth and societal progress.
 
• It ensures equal access to knowledge and skills, fostering **social equity and inclusiveness.**
 
• **Example:** Public schools and universities play a pivotal role in shaping the workforce and fostering innovation in various fields.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Distinction between Soft and Hard Infrastructure:**

 
 
• **Hard infrastructure** is tangible and includes physical structures and facilities essential for operational efficiency.
 
• **Soft infrastructure** is intangible and focuses on societal systems, institutions, and services that enhance human capital and social welfare.
 
• **Example:** Healthcare systems (soft infrastructure) complement hospital buildings (hard infrastructure) by delivering services.
 
 
 
• **Global Examples:**
 
 
• **Finland's public education system** is globally renowned for its emphasis on equity and quality.
 
• **Japan's hard infrastructure** includes advanced railways like the Shinkansen, while its soft infrastructure ensures efficient governance and societal frameworks.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the estimation of India’s national and per capita income during the colonial rule is correct?

options.text: The colonial government never made any sincere attempt to estimate India’s national and per capita income.
The colonial government estimated India’s national and per capita income sincerely every year.

The colonial government estimated India’s national income but ignored per capita income.

questions.solution:

__

questions.question: The sum of two numbers is 57 and their L.C.M. is 812. What are the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We can solve this directly using the given options.

Check the sum: All given options sum to 57.

Check the LCM for Option 3: 28 and 29 are consecutive numbers, meaning they are co-prime.

The L.C.M. of co-prime numbers is simply their product: 28 × 29 = 812.

Since this perfectly matches the given condition, we do not need to check further.

**∴ The correct answer is 28, 29.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of two numbers = 57

L.C.M. of the two numbers = 812

**Concept Used:**

Let the HCF of the numbers be h. The numbers can be written as hx and hy, where x and y are co-prime.

Sum = h(x + y) and L.C.M. = hxy

**Calculations:**

⇒ h(x + y) = 57

⇒ hxy = 812

⇒ To find the HCF (h), we check the common factors of 57 (which are 1, 3, 19, 57) and 812.

⇒ Since 812 is not divisible by 3, 19, or 57, the highest common factor h must be 1.

⇒ Therefore, the two numbers are co-prime, meaning x + y = 57 and xy = 812.

⇒ Substituting y = 57 − x into the product equation gives:

⇒ x(57 − x) = 812

⇒ x² − 57x + 812 = 0

⇒ Factorising the quadratic equation: x² − 28x − 29x + 812 = 0

⇒ x(x − 28) − 29(x − 28) = 0

⇒ (x − 28)(x − 29) = 0

⇒ The roots of the quadratic equation are x = 28 and x = 29.

**∴ The correct answer is 28, 29.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product of Numbers Rule

For any two given numbers, the product of the numbers is always equal to the product of their HCF and LCM (First Number × Second Number = HCF × LCM).

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are called co-prime if their HCF is 1. The LCM of two co-prime numbers is easily found by multiplying them together.

Consecutive Numbers Concept

Any two consecutive natural numbers (like 28 and 29) are always co-prime, meaning they will not share any common factors other than 1.
</p

questions.question: The greatest number that divides 131, 91, and 215, leaving remainders 8, 9, and 10 respectively, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Subtract the given remainders from the respective numbers: 131 − 8 = 123, 91 − 9 = 82, and 215 − 10 = 205.

To find the HCF quickly, take the difference of the two closest numbers: 123 − 82 = 41.

The greatest common divisor must be a factor of this difference.

Since 41 exactly divides all three numbers (123, 82, 205) and is a prime number, it is the required HCF.

**∴ The correct answer is 41.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers: 131, 91, and 215

Remainders: 8, 9, and 10 respectively

**Method Used:**

Required Number = HCF of (Number₁ − Remainder₁), (Number₂ − Remainder₂), and (Number₃ − Remainder₃)

**Calculations:**

⇒ First number = 131 − 8 = 123

⇒ Second number = 91 − 9 = 82

⇒ Third number = 215 − 10 = 205

⇒ Now, we find the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of 123, 82, and 205.

⇒ Prime factorization of 123 = 3 × 41

⇒ Prime factorization of 82 = 2 × 41

⇒ Prime factorization of 205 = 5 × 41

⇒ The highest common factor present in all three numbers is 41.

⇒ HCF(123, 82, 205) = 41

**∴ The correct answer is 41.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF with different remainders

If a number divides x, y, and z leaving remainders a, b, and c respectively, the greatest such number is the HCF of (x−a), (y−b), and (z−c).

HCF with same remainder

If a number divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder 'r' in each case without given value, the greatest such number is the HCF of |x−y|, |y−z|, and |z−x|.

LCM with same remainder

The smallest number which when divided by x, y, and z leaves the same remainder 'r' is given by [LCM of (x, y, z)] + r.

LCM with different remainders

If divided by x, y, z leaving remainders a, b, c respectively where (x−a) = (y−b) = (z−c) = k, the smallest number is [LCM of (x, y, z)] − k.
</p

questions.question: A man goes to Nagpur from Visakhapatnam at a speed of 55 km/hr and returns to Visakhapatnam at speed of 66 km/hr, through the same route. What is his average speed (in km/hr) of the entire journey?

When the same distance is covered at speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed formula is:

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 55 × 66) ÷ (55 + 66)

⇒ Average Speed = (7260) ÷ 121

⇒ Average Speed = 60 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Speed of onward journey (S₁) = 55 km/hr

⇒ Speed of return journey (S₂) = 66 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = D + D = 2D km

⇒ Time taken for onward journey = D ÷ 55 hours

⇒ Time taken for return journey = D ÷ 66 hours

Average Speed for 3 Equal Distances

If three equal distances are covered at speeds x, y, and z respectively, then Average Speed = (3 × x × y × z) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the value by (5 ÷ 18). Conversely, to convert m/s to km/hr, multiply the value by (18 ÷ 5).

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the same direction at speeds S₁ and S₂ (where S₁ > S₂), their Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. If they move in opposite directions, their Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

questions.question: The sum of the squares of two consecutive odd natural numbers is 394. The sum of the numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The sum of squares of the two consecutive odd numbers is 394, so their average square is 394 ÷ 2 = 197.

The perfect squares of odd numbers closest to 197 are 169 (which is 13²) and 225 (which is 15²).

Verifying their sum: 169 + 225 = 394.

Thus, the two consecutive odd natural numbers are 13 and 15.

Required sum = 13 + 15 = 28.

**∴ The correct answer is 28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The sum of the squares of two consecutive odd natural numbers is 394.

**Formula Used:**

(a − b)² + (a + b)² = 2(a² + b²)

**Calculation:**

Let the two consecutive odd natural numbers be represented as (2n − 1) and (2n + 1).

⇒ (2n − 1)² + (2n + 1)² = 394

⇒ 2[(2n)² + 1²] = 394

⇒ 4n² + 1 = 197

⇒ 4n² = 196

⇒ n² = 49

⇒ n = 7 (Since the numbers are natural numbers, n must be positive)

The sum of the two numbers is: (2n − 1) + (2n + 1) = 4n

⇒ Sum = 4 × 7 = 28

**∴ The correct answer is 28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Consecutive Odd and Even Numbers

Consecutive odd or even numbers always differ by 2. Symmetrically, they can be represented as (2n − 1) and (2n + 1) for odds, and (2n − 2), 2n, (2n + 2) for evens to simplify calculations.

Important Algebraic Identity

The algebraic identity (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²) is highly useful for rapidly simplifying problems that involve the sum of squares of terms differing by a constant value.

Quadratic Roots Nature

When a word problem on natural numbers reduces to a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the discriminant D = b² − 4ac must be a perfect square, and negative roots are rejected.

questions.question: The area of a triangle is 1080 cm² and its sides are in the ratio 5 : 12 : 13. The perimeter of the triangle is:

The ratio of the sides is 5 : 12 : 13, which forms a Pythagorean triplet indicating it is a right-angled triangle.

Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 5x × 12x = 30x²

Given area = 1080 ⇒ 30x² = 1080 ⇒ x² = 36 ⇒ x = 6

Perimeter = 5x + 12x + 13x = 30x = 30 × 6 = 180 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 180 cm.**

**Given:**

Ratio of sides = 5 : 12 : 13

Area of the triangle = 1080 cm²

**Formula Used:**

For a triangle with sides a, b, c, semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2

Area by Heron's formula = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)]

 

 
 5x (30 cm)
 12x (72 cm)
 13x (78 cm)
 Area = 1080 cm²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the sides of the triangle be 5x, 12x, and 13x.

⇒ Semi-perimeter, s = (5x + 12x + 13x) ÷ 2 = 30x ÷ 2 = 15x

⇒ Area = √[15x(15x − 5x)(15x − 12x)(15x − 13x)]

⇒ 1080 = √[15x × 10x × 3x × 2x]

⇒ 1080 = √[900x⁴]

⇒ 1080 = 30x²

⇒ x² = 1080 ÷ 30

⇒ x² = 36

⇒ x = 6

⇒ Perimeter of the triangle = 5x + 12x + 13x = 30x

⇒ Perimeter = 30 × 6 = 180 cm

Pythagorean Triplets

A set of three positive integers a, b, c that satisfy a² + b² = c². Common examples include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), and (7, 24, 25). Identifying these can instantly simplify right-angled triangle problems and skip complex formulas.

Heron's Formula

Used to calculate the area of any triangle when all three side lengths are known: Area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)], where s is the semi-perimeter.

Right-Angled Triangle Area

For a right-angled triangle, the area can be directly calculated as ½ × base × perpendicular height, bypassing the need for semi-perimeters entirely.

questions.question: simplify the given expression. x(3x − 5) + 5(x² − 3) + 16
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Directly expand the brackets and combine the like terms together.

⇒ 3x² − 5x + 5x² − 15 + 16

⇒ (3 + 5)x² − 5x + (16 − 15)

⇒ 8x² − 5x + 1

**∴ The correct answer is 8x² − 5x + 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: x(3x − 5) + 5(x² − 3) + 16

**Calculation:**

⇒ Expand the first term: x × 3x − x × 5 = 3x² − 5x

⇒ Expand the second term: 5 × x² − 5 × 3 = 5x² − 15

⇒ Substitute the expanded values back into the expression:

⇒ 3x² − 5x + 5x² − 15 + 16

⇒ Group the like terms (terms with x², terms with x, and constant terms):

⇒ (3x² + 5x²) − 5x + (−15 + 16)

⇒ 8x² − 5x + 1

**∴ The correct answer is 8x² − 5x + 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Distributive Property

The distributive property states that multiplying a sum by a number gives the same result as multiplying each addend by the number and then adding the products together: a(b + c) = a × b + a × c.

Like Terms in Algebra

Like terms are terms that have the exact same variables and exponents. Only like terms can be added or subtracted to simplify algebraic expressions. For example, 3x² and 5x² are like terms and can be added to get 8x².

BODMAS Rule

BODMAS stands for Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction. It determines the correct sequence of operations when simplifying a mathematical expression.
</p

A number divisible by 88 must be divisible by both 8 and 11.

**Given:**

Number = 91673

Divisor = 88

**Formula Used:**

Smallest number to be added = Divisor − Remainder

**Calculations:**

⇒ Divide 91673 by 88 to find the remainder.

⇒ 91673 = (88 × 1041) + 65

⇒ The remainder is 65.

⇒ Number to be added = 88 − 65

⇒ Number to be added = 23

Divisibility Rule for 88

A number is divisible by 88 if it is completely divisible by both of its co-prime factors, 8 and 11.

Divisibility Rule for 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is completely divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule for 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of its digits at odd places and the sum of its digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

Finding the Number to be Added

The smallest number to be added to a given number to make it completely divisible by a divisor is given by: Divisor − Remainder.
</p

**Therefore, conclusion (I) does not logically follow.**

**(II) All graphs are chisels:**

 The relationship is only a **'Some'** relationship (a partial overlap).
